saints.name: St. Chaeremon and the Martyrs of Egypt
saints.title: Bishop and Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: An aged Egyptian bishop and the many Christians who perished in the deserts fleeing the persecution of Decius…
biography: When the emperor Decius commanded sacrifice to the gods about the year 250, the persecution fell heavily upon the Church of Egypt. Many Christians were slain outright in the cities and villages, while others fled into the deserts and mountains rather than deny Christ, and there perished — some of hunger and thirst, some by wild beasts, some taken by robbers — and all were reckoned martyrs.

Among them was Chaeremon, the very aged bishop of Nilopolis, a city on the Nile. Fleeing with his wife into the mountain country east of the river, he was seen no more; though the brethren searched diligently, neither the two nor their bodies were ever found, and the Church numbered them with the martyrs.

These things were recorded by Dionysius of Alexandria, himself a fugitive in that persecution, in a letter to Fabius of Antioch from which the historian Eusebius preserved the account. The Roman Martyrology joins Chaeremon with the many martyrs of Egypt on 22 December.
saints.knownFor: The confessors and martyrs of the Decian persecution in Egypt.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
